title_en: Jinchang Jiuce Industrial Gas Co., Ltd. v. Gansu Fengsheng Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over processing contract
ruling_gist_en: The liquidated damages for overdue payment agreed in the contract and the delayed performance damages stipulated in the Civil Procedure Law are two different and concurrently applicable civil liabilities. After the court judgment takes effect, the breach of overdue payment continues to exist until the debt is discharged. The debtor shall continue to bear liability for breach due to overdue payment. If the creditor requests that the liquidated damages be calculated up to the date of actual discharge, the people's court shall support such request.

full_text_en:
Jinchang Jiuce Industrial Gas Co., Ltd. v. Gansu Fengsheng Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd. — processing contract dispute

【Ruling Gist】

The liquidated damages for overdue payment stipulated in the contract and the damages for delayed performance provided in the Civil Procedure Law are two different types of civil liability that may be imposed concurrently. After a court judgment takes effect, the default in overdue payment continues to exist until the debt is fully satisfied, and the debtor shall continue to bear the liability for liquidated damages for overdue payment. Where the creditor requests that the liquidated damages be calculated up to the date of actual satisfaction, the people's court shall support such request.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2022) Zui Gao Fa Min Zai No. 77

Retrial Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Jinchang Jiuce Industrial Gas Co., Ltd. Domicile: Next to Jingsan Road, Chemical Circular Economy Industrial Park, Hexibao Town, Yongchang County, Jinchang City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Xiong Zhihai, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Lin Geng, lawyer of Grandall Law Firm (Fuzhou).

Agent ad litem: Lin Xiaoyu, lawyer of Grandall Law Firm (Fuzhou).

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Gansu Fengsheng Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd. Domicile: Chemical Circular Economy Industrial Park, Hexibao Town, Yongchang County, Jinchang City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Hu, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Yongcheng, employee of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Luo Wenhu, lawyer of Gansu Zhongna Law Firm.

The retrial applicant, Jinchang Jiuce Industrial Gas Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiuce Company), having refused to accept the civil judgment (2020) Gan Min Zhong No. 143 rendered by the Gansu High People's Court in the case concerning the dispute over a processing contract with the respondent, Gansu Fengsheng Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fengsheng Company), filed an application for retrial with this Court. This Court rendered a civil ruling (2021) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 945 on April 30, 2021, granting a retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegiate bench according to law and held a public hearing of this case on March 1, 2022. The agents ad litem of the retrial applicant Jiuce Company, Lin Geng and Lin Xiaoyu, and the agents ad litem of the respondent Fengsheng Company, Zhang Yongcheng and Luo Wenhu, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The trial of this case is now concluded.

Jiuce Company applied for retrial on the following grounds: 1. Modify item 2 of the second-instance judgment, and instead order Fengsheng Company to pay Jiuce Company processing fees of RMB 8,652,289.71 for the period from October 10, 2013 to February 13, 2015, together with liquidated damages for overdue payment of RMB 5,461,480.52 calculated up to December 31, 2017 for such processing fees, and liquidated damages for overdue payment calculated at a daily rate of 0.05% based on RMB 8,652,289.71 from January 1, 2018 until the date of full payment; 2. Modify item 3 of the second-instance judgment to: Fengsheng Company shall pay Jiuce Company processing fees of RMB 22,468,215.13 for the period from February 14, 2015 to July 31, 2017 (the suspension period), together with liquidated damages for overdue payment (calculated up to December 31, 2017 as RMB 6,441,687.55, and thereafter at a daily rate of 0.05% based on RMB 22,468,215.13 until the date of full payment). 3. The litigation costs of this case shall be borne by Fengsheng Company. Facts and reasons:

(I) The second-instance judgment erred in law by adjusting the cut-off date for calculating liquidated damages for overdue payment to the date when the judgment took effect. 1. Neither party appealed against the cut-off date for calculating liquidated damages for overdue payment. The second-instance judgment adjusted that date to the date when the judgment took effect, which exceeded the scope of the appeal and violated Article 323 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "the people's court of second instance shall conduct the trial around the appeal requests of the parties. Requests not raised by the parties shall not be tried." 2. The second-instance judgment held that "the confirmation and assumption of liability for liquidated damages shall be terminated on the date when the people's court's judgment takes effect, and the failure to perform the obligations after that date shall no longer be attributable to a breach of contract." This finding has no legal basis. Fengsheng Company has not yet paid the overdue processing fees to Jiuce Company, and the state of overdue payment continues. Fengsheng Company shall pay Jiuce Company liquidated damages for overdue payment until the date of full satisfaction. 3. Liquidated damages for overdue payment and the statutory liability for delayed performance under Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2017) are two different types of liability. That provision is intended to urge the person subject to enforcement to perform the effective legal document as soon as possible; it is a statutory supplementary liability and does not conflict with the liability for breach of contract for overdue payment. There is no confusion or duplication between the two. The second-instance judgment adjusted the cut-off date for the liability for liquidated damages for overdue payment on the ground that "the first-instance judgment violated the prohibitive provisions of the law or harmed the national interest, social public interest, or the lawful rights and interests of others." This application of law was erroneous and seriously damaged the lawful rights and interests of Jiuce Company.

(II) The second-instance judgment erred in its determination of the processing fees for the suspension period and erroneously failed to grant the request for liquidated damages for overdue payment on such processing fees. 1. Jiuce Company's request that Fengsheng Company compensate it for the loss of processing fees during the suspension period based on the minimum annual processing volume has a contractual basis, and this position was repeatedly confirmed in multiple provisions of the contract. The amount of such compensation for loss was fully foreseeable at the time of contract formation and should be supported. (1) The second-instance judgment has already found that Fengsheng Company's suspension does not constitute a ground for exemption from liability and that it should bear liability for breach of contract as stipulated in the contract. The provision in Article 6.1.1 of the contract in question, regarding Fengsheng Company's obligation to pay processing fees based on the minimum annual processing volume, is essentially a method for calculating damages payable by Fengsheng Company to Jiuce Company when the actual annual processing volume falls short of the agreed amount. According to this provision, the loss of processing fees during the suspension period should be compensated based on the minimum annual processing volume. Only if the parties have not agreed on the matter should Article 113 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China on statutory damages apply. However, the second-instance judgment disregarded the parties' agreement on the amount of damages and erroneously applied that provision. (2) Article 114 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides that only upon a party's request may the court appropriately reduce the liquidated damages. In this case, Fengsheng Company never claimed that the minimum processing fee was excessively high compared to the loss actually suffered, nor did it adduce evidence to that effect. Even if Fengsheng Company had made such a request, the court should have considered whether to adjust the amount of damages under paragraph 2 of that Article. (3) The second-instance judgment regarded Jiuce Company's loss as anticipated profit and determined Jiuce Company's loss based on an annual profit margin of 20%, which lacks factual and legal basis. According to Article 113 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the losses suffered by Jiuce Company due to Fengsheng Company's breach include not only anticipated profit but also actual losses such as maintenance costs, depreciation costs, necessary administrative expenses, and employee salary expenses for the machinery and equipment during the suspension period. The second-instance court did not require Jiuce Company to adduce evidence on the project costs or on the expenses for equipment maintenance and labor during the suspension period, yet it held in the judgment that Jiuce Company bore the burden of proof for such facts, thereby erroneously increasing Jiuce Company's burden of proof. Anticipated profit and profit margin are not entirely equivalent. The second-instance judgment's finding that Jiuce Company's "appropriate profit margin" was 20% has no factual basis and exceeds the scope of discretion. 2. The second-instance judgment's failure to grant liquidated damages for overdue payment on the processing fees for the suspension period is inconsistent with the contract. There is no conflict between Article 6.1.3 and Article 6.1.1 of the contract in question. Article 6.1.1 of the processing contract provides: "Fengsheng Company shall comply with the restriction on minimum annual processing volume stipulated in Article 3.5 of Chapter 3 of this contract. If the actual annual processing volume is lower than the minimum annual processing volume, Fengsheng Company shall pay the processing fee based on the minimum annual processing volume." According to this provision, Fengsheng Company shall pay the processing fee based on the minimum annual processing volume at the agreed time. If payment is delayed, it falls within the circumstance of late payment under Article 6.1.3, and Fengsheng Company shall bear liability for liquidated damages for overdue payment.

(III) The second-instance judgment failed to distinguish the allocation of court acceptance fees between the first instance and the second instance, resulting in the amount of court acceptance fees to be borne by Jiuce Company for the first and second instances being unclear. This has so far prevented Jiuce Company from applying for a refund, and the error should be corrected.

Fengsheng Company argued in response that the retrial request of Jiuce Company should be dismissed according to law and the errors in the second-instance judgment should be corrected. (I) The second-instance judgment, in accordance with Article 323 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, adjusted the cut-off date for calculating liquidated damages for overdue payment during the normal production period to the date when the judgment took effect, which is in line with the law. (II) From February 2015 to July 2017, Fengsheng Company did not use Jiuce Company's oxygen. The reason for the suspension during this period was beyond Fengsheng Company's own control and falls within the grounds for exemption from liability agreed by the parties. Fengsheng Company should not bear liability for breach of contract, nor should it bear liquidated damages for overdue payment on the processing fees during the suspension period. 1. The suspension caused by the shortage of energy was a ground for exemption from liability under the contract, and Fengsheng Company should not be held liable. (1) The second chapter of the processing contract, "Cooperation Background," clearly states that Fengsheng Company's chemical plant is in the middle of the circular economy chain. In this case, the coke oven gas supplied by Inner Mongolia Taixi Coal Group Jinchang Xinhua Coking Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinhua Coking Company) to Fengsheng Company serves both as energy fuel and raw material, falling within the category of "energy" under the contract's exemption clause. The first-instance court's finding that the shortage of raw material gas constitutes an exemption from liability under the contract was not improper. (2) The inability of Xinhua Coking Company to supply coke oven gas was due to the nationwide downturn in the coal chemical industry and severe accumulation of coke inventories, not because of Fengsheng Company's arrears in payment. Coke oven gas is a by-product of Xinhua Coking Company's coke production; apart from its limited own use, it can only be supplied to downstream users or flared. (3) The first-instance judgment correctly found that Fengsheng Company's failure to use Jiuce Company's oxygen fell within the exemption clause under Article 6.3 of the processing contract, while the second-instance judgment erroneously found that the cessation of oxygen use did not constitute an exemption from liability. If Jiuce Company's claim were supported, it would enable Jiuce Company to obtain more benefits without organizing production than if it had actually produced, which is manifestly unfair. During the period from February 2015 to July 2017, Jiuce Company did not process any gas, and thus the loss for breach cannot be calculated based on the minimum annual processing volume. The 20% profit margin was an estimate by Jiuce Company's agent and lacks factual support. Fengsheng Company does not agree with the second-instance judgment but, due to its difficult financial situation and inability to pay the relevant costs, did not apply for a retrial itself. 2. As stated above, the suspension period falls within the exemption clause agreed in the contract. Fengsheng Company should not bear the processing fees for the suspension period, and thus should not bear the liquidated damages for overdue payment on such fees.

Jiuce Company filed the following claims in the first-instance court: Fengsheng Company shall pay Jiuce Company processing fees of RMB 31,121,888.04 and liquidated damages of RMB 11,903,897.01, totaling RMB 43,025,785.05. During the proceedings, Jiuce Company amended its claims to: 1. Fengsheng Company shall pay Jiuce Company processing fees of RMB 31,120,504.84; 2. Fengsheng Company shall pay Jiuce Company liquidated damages for overdue payment of RMB 11,903,168.07 calculated up to December 31, 2017 at a daily rate of 0.05%; 3. Fengsheng Company shall pay Jiuce Company liquidated damages calculated at a daily rate of 0.05% based on RMB 31,120,504.84 from January 1, 2018 until the date of full payment of the processing fees.

The first-instance court found the following facts: On October 1, 2010, Gansu Jinchang Chemical Industry Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinhua Company) and Fujian Jiuce Industrial Gas Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fujian Jiuce Company) entered into the "Oxygen Processing Contract for the Air Separation Unit Supporting Jinhua Company's 200,000-ton Synthetic Ammonia and 300,000-ton Urea Project," stipulating that: Fujian Jiuce Company would provide oxygen and nitrogen for the 200,000-ton synthetic ammonia and 300,000-ton urea project of Jinhua Company in the Chemical Circular Economy Industrial Park in Hexibao Town; Jinhua Company would provide Fujian Jiuce Company with construction land and provide the required dual-circuit power supply and purified cooling water to the newly established company of Fujian Jiuce Company. The newly established gas company of Fujian Jiuce Company would be responsible for investing, constructing, and managing the air separation unit, including air compressors, oxygen compressors, and other supporting facilities, processing oxygen and nitrogen for Jinhua Company and delivering them according to Jinhua Company's requirements. The maximum annual oxygen processing volume for Jinhua Company by the newly established gas company of Fujian Jiuce Company would be 39.6 million Nm3 (calculated based on hourly processing of 5,000 Nm3 of oxygen, 24 hours a day, 330 processing days per year); the minimum would be 38.41 million Nm3 (calculated based on hourly processing of 4,850 Nm3 of oxygen, 24 hours a day, 330 processing days per year). The remaining gas products generated during the processing process would belong to the newly established company of Fujian Jiuce Company. The settlement price for oxygen processing fees was RMB 0.235/Nm3 (tax included), and the processing fees would be settled monthly. The settlement method was that the parties would confirm the previous month's electricity consumption, water consumption, oxygen supply volume, and processing fees by the 5th of each month. The newly established company of Fujian Jiuce Company would issue a VAT invoice for the processing fees the day after confirmation, and Jinhua Company would pay the previous month's processing fees by bank transfer within 5 days after receiving the invoice. Jinhua Company should strictly comply with the restriction on minimum annual processing volume. If the actual annual processing volume was lower than the minimum annual processing volume, Jinhua Company should pay the processing fee based on the minimum annual processing volume. Jinhua Company should pay the processing fee promptly as agreed in the contract. If payment was delayed, the newly established company of Fujian Jiuce Company had the right to stop processing oxygen for Jinhua Company and had the right to charge Jinhua Company a daily late payment penalty of 0.05% of the overdue amount. Where a party was unable to perform its contractual obligations due to force majeure as provided by law or to shortages of electricity, energy, or transportation or public utilities beyond that party's control, that party would not bear liability for breach of contract arising therefrom, but must notify the other party in writing within 24 hours to avoid the expansion of loss. The contract term was from October 1, 2010 to September 30, 2025.

On March 15, 2012, Fujian Jiuce Company, Jinhua Company, Jiuce Company, and Fengsheng Company entered into the "Supplementary Agreement to the Oxygen Processing Contract for the Air Separation Unit Supporting Jinhua Company's 200,000-ton Synthetic Ammonia and 300,000-ton Urea Project," stipulating that: Jinhua Company and Fujian Jiuce Company would no longer perform the original contract; instead, Jiuce Company and Fengsheng Company would perform the original contract. After the contract was signed, Fengsheng Company provided Jiuce Company with the electricity and purified cooling water required for production, and Jiuce Company used its production equipment to process oxygen for Fengsheng Company.

During the period from October 10, 2013 to February 13, 2015, Fengsheng Company failed to pay the processing fees for the previous month within 5 days after receiving the invoice, and accumulated overdue processing fees of RMB 8,652,289.71 to Jiuce Company. According to the agreed interest rate, the interest for overdue payment calculated up to December 31, 2017 on this amount was RMB 5,462,209.46. Fengsheng Company was located in the mid-to-downstream of the circular economy chain in the Hexibao Town Circular Economy Industrial Park, using the waste gas from Xinhua Coking Company's coke production as raw material to produce synthetic ammonia. On February 12, 2015, Xinhua Coking Company informed Fengsheng Company by letter that it could not provide the raw material gas required for production. The main content of the letter was: Due to Fengsheng Company's arrears of over RMB 50 million in payments, arrears of over RMB 30 million owed by other entities, a sustained market downturn, an inventory of 180,000 tons of coke, and RMB 230 million in funds tied up by Xinhua Coking Company, resulting in a severe shortage of working capital; affected by the economic downturn, some coal washing plants had suspended operations, and Xinhua Coking Company's stock of raw coal was insufficient at less than 60,000 tons, making it unable to maintain normal production and forced to reduce production and decrease load. It could not guarantee subsequent gas supply. It would consider resuming gas supply only after production load was restored. This measure was taken out of necessity and requested Fengsheng Company's understanding.

Xinhua Coking Company was scheduled to stop supplying gas to Fengsheng Company at 8:00 a.m. on February 13, 2015. On that day, Fengsheng Company notified Jiuce Company in writing to stop supplying oxygen to Fengsheng Company. From February 14, 2015 to July 31, 2017, Jiuce Company no longer supplied oxygen to Fengsheng Company. Calculated based on the agreed minimum annual gas supply volume of 38.41 million Nm3, the processing fee for this period was RMB 22.1146 million.

The first-instance court found that, as to whether Fengsheng Company's cessation of receiving oxygen from Jiuce Company fell within the contractual exemption from liability for breach of contract: The parties agreed in the contract that "where a party is unable to perform its contractual obligations due to force majeure as provided by law or to shortages of electricity, energy, or transportation or public utilities beyond that party's control, that party shall not bear liability for breach of contract arising therefrom." Although this clause only lists "inability to obtain electricity and energy, and shortages of transportation and public utilities" as grounds for exemption, the clause also includes "or other causes beyond a party's control" after listing these four types. According to the literal meaning of this clause, the grounds for exemption should also include factors of production that are equivalent in function to electricity, energy, transportation, and public utilities and are beyond a party's control. Fengsheng Company was located in the mid-to-downstream of the circular economy chain in the Hexibao Town Circular Economy Industrial Park, using the waste gas from Xinhua Coking Company's coke production as raw material, and had no other means to obtain raw material gas. Raw material gas is a factor of production equivalent in function to electricity, energy, transportation, and public utilities. Fengsheng Company could not control the supply of raw materials from upstream enterprises, and therefore the shortage of raw material gas constituted a ground for exemption from liability for breach of contract.

As to whether the agreed daily rate of 0.05% for liquidated damages for overdue payment was excessively high compared to the losses caused by Fengsheng Company's breach to Jiuce Company: The daily rate of 0.05% corresponds to an annual rate of 18.25%. Although this agreed rate exceeded the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period, the cost of borrowing or the return on lending in real economic life is often higher than that benchmark rate. Therefore, the benchmark rate cannot be used as the sole criterion for measuring the other party's losses due to overdue payment. Fengsheng Company's argument that the benchmark rate should be used to determine Jiuce Company's losses lacks sufficient basis. The agreement on a daily rate of 0.05% does not exceed the upper limit of 24% per annum for private lending under the law and also conforms to the expectations of the parties at the time of contract formation. Therefore, calculating liquidated damages for overdue payment at a daily rate of 0.05% is commensurate with the losses caused to Jiuce Company by Fengsheng Company's breach, and the standard of a daily rate of 0.05% should be used to determine Jiuce Company's losses.

The processing contract signed between JiuCe Company and FengSheng Company is legally valid and effective. FengSheng Company shall pay JiuCe Company the outstanding processing fees for the period from October 10, 2013 to February 13, 2015 in the amount of RMB 8,652,289.71, and shall pay liquidated damages for late payment of such arrears at a daily rate of 0.05%. The cessation of acceptance of oxygen supplied by JiuCe Company by FengSheng Company from February 14, 2015 to July 31, 2017 was due to the exempting cause of shortage of production raw materials. Therefore, FengSheng Company is not liable for the liability for breach of contract for paying processing fees based on the minimum annual gas supply volume of 38,410,000 Nm3. The liquidated damages for late payment agreed upon by the parties are commensurate with the losses caused to JiuCe Company by FengSheng Company's breach of contract. The court of first instance did not sustain FengSheng Company's argument for adjustment of the liquidated damages.

In summary, in accordance with Articles 107, 114, and 263 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 29 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (II), the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: 1. FengSheng Company shall pay JiuCe Company processing fees of RMB 8,652,289.71 for the period from October 10, 2013 to February 13, 2015, liquidated damages for late payment of such processing fees calculated up to December 31, 2017 in the amount of RMB 5,461,480.52, and liquidated damages for late payment from January 1, 2018 until the date of full payment of such processing fees, calculated at a daily rate of 0.05%, to be performed within thirty days after this judgment takes effect; 2. JiuCe Company's other claims are dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 256,918 shall be borne by JiuCe Company in the amount of RMB 172,138 and by FengSheng Company in the amount of RMB 84,780.

JiuCe Company appealed, requesting: to set aside item 2 of the first-instance judgment, and to amend the judgment to order FengSheng Company to pay JiuCe Company processing fees for the period of suspension from February 13, 2015 to July 31, 2017 in the amount of RMB 22,468,215.13, together with liquidated damages for late payment of such processing fees tentatively calculated to December 31, 2017 at a daily rate of 0.05% in the amount of RMB 6,441,687.55, and thereafter continue to calculate liquidated damages at a daily rate of 0.05% based on the principal of RMB 22,468,215.13 until the date of full payment, and to order FengSheng Company to bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances.

The court of second instance found upon trial that the synthetic ammonia and oxygen processing projects involved in the case had both resumed production on August 1, 2017. According to the "Application for Amendment of Claims" submitted by JiuCe Company in the retrial of the first instance, the processing fees owed by FengSheng Company to JiuCe Company for the period from October 10, 2013 to February 13, 2015 should be reduced from the originally claimed RMB 8,653,672.91 by the amount of water fees of RMB 1,383.20, resulting in RMB 8,652,289.71. The liquidated damages for late payment of such processing fees accrued to December 31, 2017 should be RMB 5,461,480.52, after deducting the corresponding liquidated damages of RMB 728.94 for the water fees, rather than the amount of RMB 5,462,209.46 confirmed in the fact-finding portion of the first-instance judgment. Other facts found by the second instance are essentially consistent with those of the first instance.

The court of second instance held that the processing contract involved in the case, signed by JiuCe Company and FengSheng Company, represented the true intentions of both parties, its content did not violate any mandatory provisions of laws or regulations, was legally valid and effective, and should be confirmed. Both parties shall perform their obligations and bear corresponding liabilities in accordance with the contract. For the period from October 10, 2013 to February 13, 2015, FengSheng Company owed JiuCe Company processing fees of RMB 8,652,289.71 and liquidated damages for late payment of such processing fees up to December 31, 2017 of RMB 5,461,480.52. Both parties had no dispute over this fact, and the court of second instance confirmed it. Regarding the liquidated damages for late payment of such processing fees from January 1, 2018 onwards, the first-instance judgment confirmed the period for performance as until the date of actual payment of such amount. Liquidated damages are a method of bearing liability for breach of contract as agreed in the contract. The confirmation and bearing of such liability should terminate on the date the court judgment takes effect. Thereafter, failure to perform obligations in accordance with the judgment is no longer characterized as a breach of contract, and the method of bearing liability is no longer payment of liquidated damages, but rather bearing the statutory liability for delayed performance for failure to perform the obligation to pay as specified in an effective legal instrument, in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (revised in 2017). The first-instance judgment confirmed that the liquidated damages for late payment for this period were to be paid until the date of actual repayment, causing confusion, duplication, and conflict between the two different stages of liability forms and their bearing methods. Although FengSheng Company did not appeal this point, in accordance with Article 323 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "the people's court of second instance shall conduct the trial based on the parties' claims on appeal. Matters not raised by the parties in their appeal shall not be tried, except where the first-instance judgment violates a mandatory prohibition of law, or harms national interests, public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of others," the court of second instance corrected this issue.

Regarding the issue of whether the fact that FengSheng Company ceased using oxygen from JiuCe Company due to the suspension and reduction of supply of coke oven gas by the third party Xinhua Coking Chemical Company constituted an exempting cause under Article 6.3 of the processing contract involved in the case. Article 125(1) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where there is a dispute between the parties over the understanding of a contract term, the true meaning of that term shall be determined in accordance with the words and sentences used in the contract, the relevant provisions of the contract, the purpose of the contract, trade practices, and the principle of good faith." In this case, the provision of Article 6.3 of the processing contract signed by JiuCe Company and FengSheng Company is the main point of divergence between the parties. According to the aforementioned legal provisions, the analysis is as follows:

From the perspective of textual interpretation of the contract, in this provision, "force majeure as provided by law" and "causes beyond a party's control" are connected by the word "and," indicating that they are two alternative constitutive elements that jointly serve as grounds for exemption from liability for breach of contract, in a parallel relationship. Within "causes beyond a party's control," it is further limited by way of enumeration to two situations: "inability to obtain electricity, energy" or "shortage of transportation, public utilities," followed by the word "etc." as a catch-all. Since "electricity, energy, transportation, and public utilities" are all government public infrastructure, and their supply and shortage are characterized by "unforeseeability, unavoidability, and insurmountability," the word "etc." should refer to similar or equivalent events or circumstances comparable to "inability to obtain electricity, energy" or "shortage of transportation, public utilities." Therefore, Article 6.3 adopts a strict limitation on "causes beyond a party's control," and it cannot be construed broadly. FengSheng Company argued that coke oven gas is a "fuel" and falls under "energy" listed in "causes beyond a party's control" in Article 6.3. However, multiple documents issued by relevant government departments of Gansu Province or Jinchang City concerning the project involved in the case, submitted by FengSheng Company in the first instance, all state that coke oven gas is a "raw material." Therefore, its claim cannot be sustained.

From the perspective of interpreting the purpose of the contract and the principle of good faith, JiuCe Company is an oxygen processing company established by Fujian JiuCe Company specifically in Jinchang for the synthetic ammonia project involved in the case. The purpose of signing the processing contract was to obtain a return on investment by long-term and stable processing of oxygen for FengSheng Company. FengSheng Company's purpose in signing the processing contract was to secure a long-term and stable supply of oxygen to ensure the normal operation of its synthetic ammonia project. Therefore, the processing contract involved in the case imposes strict and reciprocal provisions on the liability for breach of contract for both parties. To avoid falling into a state of uncertainty during the performance of the contract, neither party to the case could accept an unlimited expansive interpretation of "causes beyond a party's control" as provided in Article 6.3 of the contract.

The third party Xinhua Coking Chemical Company had signed a "Coke Oven Gas Supply Agreement" with FengSheng Company. The "Work Liaison Letter" issued by Xinhua Coking Chemical Company on February 12, 2015, indicated that FengSheng Company had owed Xinhua Coking Chemical Company a total of RMB 50 million for coke and gas since October 2012, accounting for 63% of Xinhua Coking Chemical Company's external trade receivables of RMB 80 million. FengSheng Company admitted that the RMB 50 million remained unpaid to date. The "Work Liaison Letter" also indicated that "the refusal to advance credit for raw coal to the still-operating coal washing plant, resulting in insufficient raw coal reserves for Xinhua Coking Chemical Company," was one of the main reasons for its production reduction and load decrease, and FengSheng Company's large overdue debt undoubtedly had a negative impact on Xinhua Coking Chemical Company's ability to purchase raw coal for production. Given that the "Coke Oven Gas Supply Agreement" signed between FengSheng Company and Xinhua Coking Chemical Company clearly stipulated the rights and obligations of both parties and pre-regulated the risk of interruption of coke oven gas supply through liability for breach of contract clauses, the shortage of raw material gas should be a commercial risk that FengSheng Company could foresee and could take measures to avoid or overcome, and is not a "cause beyond a party's control" as stipulated in Article 6.3 of the processing contract. If such conduct that is controllable or for which recourse may be had were to be treated as a "cause beyond a party's control" and thereby lead to exemption from liability, then the provisions of Article 3.5 of the processing contract concerning the minimum annual processing volume limit, and Article 6.1.1 concerning the method of payment of fees when the actual annual processing volume is lower than the minimum annual processing volume, would lose their necessity, contrary to the purpose and original intention of the parties in entering into the contract, and also contrary to the judicial orientation of building a trustworthy society and optimizing the business environment.

FengSheng Company argues that the suspension and reduction of supply of raw material gas by the upstream enterprise in the circular economy chain, forcing the downstream enterprise to suspend production, is an inherent fatal weakness of the circular economy chain in the circular industrial park, and does not constitute a breach of contract. This argument precisely demonstrates that FengSheng Company could fully foresee the commercial risks that may arise from the interruption of supply at a certain link in the circular economy chain. Therefore, when FengSheng Company signed the "Coke Oven Gas Supply Agreement" with Xinhua Coking Chemical Company, which had an indefinite cooperation term, and when it signed the processing contract involved in the case with JiuCe Company, it should have taken such foreseeable commercial risks into account. However, when the processing contract was signed, it did not explicitly include "shortage of raw material gas" as an exempting cause.

In summary, the fact that FengSheng Company ceased using oxygen from JiuCe Company due to the suspension and reduction of supply of coke oven gas by the third party Xinhua Coking Chemical Company does not constitute an exempting cause under Article 6.3 of the processing contract involved in the case. FengSheng Company shall bear liability for breach of contract towards JiuCe Company. The first-instance judgment was erroneous in this finding, and the court of second instance corrects it.

Regarding the issue of whether FengSheng Company shall pay JiuCe Company the processing fees for the period of suspension from February 14, 2015 to July 31, 2017. The synthetic ammonia processing project involved in the case actually commenced in October 2013, and was suspended from February 2015 to July 2017 for a total of 29 months. As stated above, JiuCe Company is a gas processing enterprise established by Fujian JiuCe Company specifically in Jinchang City to supply oxygen for FengSheng Company's synthetic ammonia project. According to the processing contract, the company must first satisfy the oxygen needs for FengSheng Company's production before it can dispose of any surplus gas on its own. Therefore, for JiuCe Company, which was established specifically for FengSheng Company and derived 80% of its revenue from the oxygen processing project involved in the case, it would inevitably suffer losses in the event of a suspension of its oxygen processing project due to FengSheng Company's breach of contract. Article 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If a party fails to perform its obligations under a contract, or renders performance non-conforming to the agreement, it shall bear the liability for breach of contract such as continuing performance, taking remedial measures, or compensating for losses." Article 113 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If a party fails to perform its obligations under a contract, or renders performance non-conforming to the agreement, thereby causing losses to the other party, the amount of compensation for losses shall be equivalent to the losses caused by the breach, including the benefits obtainable after the performance of the contract, but shall not exceed the losses that the breaching party foresaw or ought to have foreseen at the time of entering into the contract as possible consequences of the breach." Due to the special nature of JiuCe Company's establishment, Articles 3.5, 4.1, and 6.1.1 of the processing contract involved in the case contain restrictive clauses with a minimum guarantee nature regarding the minimum annual processing volume. However, from the perspective of overall interpretation of the contract, the aforementioned provisions should be regulations governing performance during the normal term of the contract. During the suspension period, JiuCe Company did not actually process oxygen. Under such circumstances, if payment is still to be made based on the oxygen processing fees during normal processing, it would not be consistent with the actual facts of this case. However, when FengSheng Company, without breach by JiuCe Company, unilaterally ceased using the oxygen processed by JiuCe Company, causing its suspension and losses, FengSheng Company shall bear corresponding liability for breach of contract, including payment of the expected benefits obtainable after normal performance of the contract, i.e., the profit after deducting costs, expenses, and other expenditures from the processing income. Although the "Audit Report" submitted by JiuCe Company indicated that its operating costs included selling expenses, financial expenses, and impairment losses on assets, the company did not provide evidence for the above cost items and other expenditures such as equipment maintenance and labor costs during the suspension period it claimed on appeal. Under these circumstances, the court of second instance, by reference to the normal processing fees of the processing project involved in the case during the suspension period, calculated the expected benefits at an appropriate profit margin. This constitutes the processing fees that JiuCe Company could obtain during the suspension period.

The fact-finding portion of the first-instance judgment confirmed that the processing fees for the suspension period from February 14, 2015 to July 31, 2017 were RMB 22.1146 million. JiuCe Company objected to this amount, arguing that it should be RMB 22,468,215.13 as requested in its appeal. FengSheng Company also disagreed, on the grounds that it was exempt from liability and should not bear the processing fees for the suspension period. According to the court trial investigation, the processing project involved in the case was suspended on February 14, 2015, for 15 days in that month. The suspension lasted 29 months from March 1, 2015 to July 31, 2017. Based on the contractually agreed 28 days per month, the total suspension period is 827 days. Calculated based on the minimum oxygen processing volume of 4,850 Nm3 per hour stipulated in Article 3.5 of the contract, if normal production had occurred during this period, the processing fees generated would be 4,850 Nm3/hour x 24 hours x RMB 0.235/Nm3 x 827 days = RMB 22,621,758. However, since JiuCe Company only claimed RMB 22,468,215.13, the court of second instance uses this as the basis to confirm that, under normal production conditions, FengSheng Company should pay JiuCe Company processing fees of RMB 22,468,215.13 for the period from February 14, 2015 to July 31, 2017. JiuCe Company stated during the second-instance trial that its annual profit margin was approximately 20%. Based on this statement and the profit margin reflected in the "Audit Report" submitted by the company, the court of second instance, in its discretion, calculates the expected benefits that JiuCe Company could obtain during the suspension period as 20% of the base amount of RMB 22,468,215.13, amounting to RMB 4,493,643.03.

Article 6.1.3 of the processing contract involved in the case stipulates: If FengSheng Company delays payment of processing fees, JiuCe Company has the right to cease processing oxygen for it and charge a late fee of 0.05% per day on the overdue amount. This provision governs FengSheng Company's liability for late payment under normal production conditions where delayed payment occurs. During the suspension period, JiuCe Company did not actually engage in production. In the absence of evidence submitted by JiuCe Company to prove its other actual losses during this period, the aforementioned expected benefits (processing fees) constitute compensation for its suspension losses. This amount is a specific method for FengSheng Company to bear liability for breach of contract, and is not the overdue payment referred to in Article 6.1.3 of the processing contract. Therefore, the court of second instance does not sustain JiuCe Company's appeal request for liquidated damages for late payment on the processing fees during the suspension period, calculated from February 13, 2015 at a daily rate of 0.05% until the date of actual payment.

Regarding FengSheng Company's argument that the liquidated damages calculated at a daily rate of 0.05% are excessively higher than the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China during the same period and should be adjusted. Liquidated damages are a constraint method agreed upon in advance for potential future breach. Its function is to maintain contract transactions, improve the rate of contract performance, and serve as a guarantee for contract performance, with a certain punitive nature. Article 91 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides that the party asserting a change, extinguishment, or impediment to a legal relationship shall bear the burden of proof for the basic facts of such change, extinguishment, or impediment. FengSheng Company claims that the liquidated damages are excessively high and requests an adjustment. This is essentially a request to alter the mutual agreement, but it has not submitted evidence that the liquidated damages at a daily rate of 0.05% are excessively higher than the actual losses caused to JiuCe Company by its delayed payment. Article 29 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (II) provides that if a party claims that the agreed liquidated damages are excessively high and requests an appropriate reduction, the people's court shall make a ruling based on the actual losses, taking into account comprehensive factors such as the performance of the contract, the degree of fault of the parties, and the expected benefits, measured in accordance with the principles of fairness and good faith. In this case, FengSheng Company failed to perform its obligations under the processing contract fully and on time before the suspension, and still owes processing fees of RMB 8,652,289.71 for that period. Subsequently, it caused the suspension of JiuCe Company's operations due to its unilateral breach of contract. Its conduct violates the principle of good faith and involves significant fault. Therefore, FengSheng Company's claim for adjustment of the liquidated damages in this case cannot be sustained, and the court of second instance does not support it.

In summary, part of the appeal of JiuCe Company was founded and should be supported. In accordance with Article 107, Article 113, Paragraph 1 of Article 125, and Article 263 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 29 of the Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 323 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Subparagraph 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2017), the judgment of the court of second instance was as follows: 1. Affirm Item 2 of the civil judgment (2019) Gan 03 Min Chu No. 17 of the Jinchang Intermediate People's Court of Gansu Province, i.e., dismiss the other claims of JiuCe Company. 2. Amend Item 1 of the civil judgment (2019) Gan 03 Min Chu No. 17 of the Jinchang Intermediate People's Court of Gansu Province to read: FengSheng Company shall pay JiuCe Company processing fees of RMB 8,652,289.71 for the period from October 10, 2013 to February 13, 2015, overdue payment liquidated damages of RMB 5,461,480.52 for such processing fees up to December 31, 2017, and overdue payment liquidated damages at a daily interest rate of 0.05% from January 1, 2018 to the date of entry into force of this judgment, to be performed within thirty days after the date of entry into force of this judgment; 3. FengSheng Company shall pay JiuCe Company processing fees of RMB 4,493,643.03 for the period of suspension of production from February 14, 2015 to July 31, 2017, within thirty days after the date of entry into force of this judgment. The court fee of first instance was RMB 256,918, and the court fee of second instance was RMB 256,918, totaling RMB 513,836, of which JiuCe Company shall bear RMB 154,150.80 and FengSheng Company shall bear RMB 359,685.20.

During the retrial, JiuCe Company submitted its 2019 and 2020 annual audit reports and partial financial statements, proving that in 2019, the second complete fiscal year after resumption of production, the company's operating revenue was approximately RMB 15.85 million and net profit was approximately RMB 5.7 million; in 2020, the third complete fiscal year after resumption of production, JiuCe Company's operating revenue was approximately RMB 17.97 million and net profit was approximately RMB 6.11 million. The above evidence, combined with the audit reports for 2014 through 2018 submitted by JiuCe Company in the original trial, proves that JiuCe Company had substantial operating revenue and profit during normal production periods. During the suspension period in 2016, net profit was negative over RMB 6.48 million. After offsetting gains and losses against the lowest annual net profit year in recent years, the loss amounted to over RMB 9.33 million. Therefore, the sum of losses during the suspension period and profits during normal production periods far exceeded the processing fee corresponding to the lowest annual processing volume during normal production periods, and the loss compensation stipulated in the contract was lower than the actual loss.

FengSheng Company, in its cross-examination, argued that the audit reports and financial statements lacked the signature of the person in charge of finance, and the attached accountant qualification certificates and accounting firm qualification certificates did not indicate an expiration date. Therefore, it did not recognize the legality of the above evidence, claimed that the evidence could not be used as valid evidence, and did not accept the purpose of proof.

This court will comprehensively determine the above evidence submitted by JiuCe Company in the reasoning part in conjunction with the facts of this case.

Opinion of the Court: The issues in this retrial are: 1. Whether the court of second instance erred in applying the law by adjusting the cutoff date for calculating overdue payment liquidated damages for processing fees during normal production periods payable by FengSheng Company to JiuCe Company to the date of entry into force of the judgment; 2. Whether the court of second instance erred in determining the processing fees during the suspension period and in not supporting overdue payment liquidated damages for processing fees during the suspension period.

(1) The court of second instance erred in applying the law by adjusting the cutoff date for calculating overdue payment liquidated damages to the date of entry into force of the judgment. JiuCe Company's retrial claim to have the liquidated damages calculated up to the date of actual payment is established, and this court supports it. The specific analysis is as follows:

The judgment of first instance ordered FengSheng Company to pay JiuCe Company the processing fees overdue during normal production periods and the overdue payment liquidated damages on such processing fees calculated up to the date of payment. Where neither party appealed the overdue payment liquidated damages, the court of second instance, relying on the proviso in Article 323 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China that "The people's court of second instance shall conduct the trial on the basis of the claims on appeal. Claims not raised on appeal shall not be tried, except where the judgment of first instance violates mandatory provisions of law or harms national interests, social public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of others," adjusted the cutoff date for the overdue payment liquidated damages. However, the content of the judgment of first instance regarding overdue payment liquidated damages did not violate any mandatory provisions of law, nor did it harm national interests, social public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of others; therefore, it did not meet the circumstances specified in the proviso of that article. The court of second instance erred in applying the above provision to modify the cutoff date for calculating overdue payment liquidated damages, and this court corrects that error.

Overdue payment liquidated damages and the statutory liability for delay in performance under Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2017) are two different types of liability. The liability for overdue payment for breach of contract arises from the agreement of the parties and is triggered by the fact of overdue payment. The statutory liability for delay in performance is a form of indirect enforcement, with both compensatory and punitive functions, aimed at urging the person subject to enforcement to timely perform the obligations determined by effective legal documents. The statutory liability for delay in performance differs from the liability for overdue payment for breach of contract determined by the effective judgment in terms of legal basis, nature, and scope of application. Liability for statutory delay in performance does not replace liability for overdue payment for breach of contract. Furthermore, according to Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in Calculating the Debt Interest during the Period of Delay in Performance in Enforcement Proceedings, which states that "the debt interest during the period of delay in performance after double calculation," the general debt interest during the period of delay in performance is calculated according to the method determined by the effective legal document. If liquidated damages are awarded up to the date of entry into force of the judgment, they can only be calculated up to that date; thereafter, only delay damages can be calculated at a daily rate of 0.0175% based on the overdue processing fee. This would result in the liability for delaying performance of the effective judgment being lower than the liability for breach of contract agreed by the parties, which is contrary to the contract. The fact of overdue payment existed continuously until FengSheng Company paid the processing fees. The court of second instance determined that the confirmation and assumption of liability for breach of contract ended on the date the court's judgment became effective, and thereafter the liability was statutory liability for delay in performance. There was no legal basis for modifying the cutoff date for calculating liquidated damages, and this should be corrected. The judgment of first instance, in accordance with JiuCe Company's claims, ordered that the overdue payment liquidated damages be calculated up to the date of actual payment of the processing fees, which is consistent with the contract and the law.

(2) Whether the court of second instance erred in determining the processing fees during the suspension period and in not supporting overdue payment liquidated damages for processing fees during the suspension period

1. Regarding the determination of processing fees during the suspension period

JiuCe Company argued in the retrial that the processing fees during the suspension period should be determined based on the minimum annual processing volume agreed in the processing contract. FengSheng Company defended that the suspension was a ground for exemption under the contract, so it should not bear liability. Therefore, the determination of processing fees during the suspension period includes the following issues:

(1) Whether FengSheng Company should bear liability for ceasing to take delivery of gases

According to the facts found in the original trial, FengSheng Company was situated in the middle and lower reaches of the circular economy chain of the Hexi Fort Circular Economy Industrial Park. It used the waste gas from the production of coke by Xinhua Coking Company to produce synthetic ammonia. Xinhua Coking Company's cessation of gas supply prevented FengSheng Company from obtaining production raw materials, forcing it to stop taking delivery of oxygen supplied by JiuCe Company. The content of the letter from Xinhua Coking Company to FengSheng Company regarding the cessation of gas supply indicated that the suspension of coke oven gas supply was caused by multiple factors. These included the occupation of Xinhua Coking Company's funds due to arrears in payment by FengSheng Company and other entities, persistently low market conditions, and inventory backlog of coke, as well as the economic downturn causing some coal washing plants to suspend production and insufficient stock of raw material coal to maintain normal production. FengSheng Company argued that ceasing to take delivery of oxygen was due to reasons beyond its control. According to Article 6.3 of the processing contract in question, which states that "If a party fails to perform its contractual obligations due to force majeure as provided by law or reasons beyond the control of such party, such as inability to obtain electricity, energy, or transportation, or shortage of public utilities, such party shall not be liable for the resulting liability for breach of contract," it should not bear liability for breach of contract. The court of second instance interpreted this clause from the perspectives of literal interpretation, teleological interpretation of the contract, and the principle of good faith, and held that "reasons beyond the control of such party" should not be broadly interpreted, which is not improper. FengSheng Company knew its position in the circular economy chain and that insufficient supply of raw materials from upstream enterprises would affect its production, but it did not include insufficient supply of raw material gas from third parties as a ground for exemption from liability for breach of contract. Moreover, Xinhua Coking Company's cessation of gas supply was partly due to FengSheng Company's arrears in payment. Therefore, FengSheng Company's cessation of taking delivery of oxygen does not fall within the contractual exemption clause, and FengSheng Company's defense that it should not bear liability cannot be sustained.

According to the processing contract signed by the parties, JiuCe Company was an oxygen processing company specifically established for FengSheng Company's synthetic ammonia project. Its purpose in signing the processing contract was to obtain a return on investment by processing oxygen for FengSheng Company on a long-term and stable basis. FengSheng Company's cessation of taking delivery of oxygen from JiuCe Company violated the contractual agreement that FengSheng Company would take delivery of gases. Pursuant to Article 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "If a party fails to perform its contractual obligations, or its performance fails to satisfy the terms of the contract, it shall bear the liability for breach of contract, such as to continue to perform its obligations, to take remedial measures, or to compensate for losses," FengSheng Company shall bear liability for breach of contract.

(2) Whether JiuCe Company's claim for processing fees during the suspension period based on the minimum annual processing volume was established

JiuCe Company argued that the processing fees during the suspension period should be determined based on the minimum annual processing volume agreed in the processing contract. However, according to the contract, the minimum annual processing volume was a limitation on the processing volume during the normal performance period of the contract, aimed at ensuring JiuCe Company's stable income during normal production through compensation. During the suspension period, JiuCe Company did not process gases. Its claim for processing fees during the suspension period on the basis of the limitation on minimum annual processing volume during the normal performance period lacked factual basis, and this court does not support it.

(3) Determination of the amount of damages for JiuCe Company's losses

JiuCe Company's claim for processing fees during the suspension period based on the processing fee corresponding to the minimum annual processing volume was essentially a claim for the losses caused to it by FengSheng Company's cessation of taking delivery of gases. Therefore, where JiuCe Company's claim for processing fees during the suspension period is not supported, the amount of damages for JiuCe Company's losses should be further determined.

Paragraph 1 of Article 114 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The parties may agree that upon breach of contract by one party, such party shall pay a certain amount of liquidated damages to the other party in light of the breach, or may agree on a method for calculating the amount of damages for losses arising from the breach." However, the contract in question did not contain any agreement on liability for breach or method for calculating damages during the suspension period. Therefore, JiuCe Company's losses should be determined in accordance with Article 113 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "If a party fails to perform its contractual obligations or its performance fails to satisfy the terms of the contract and causes losses to the other party, the amount of damages for losses shall be equal to the losses caused by the breach." The court of second instance applied this provision to determine the amount of JiuCe Company's damages, and its application of law was not improper.

During the proceedings of second instance, the Audit Report submitted by JiuCe Company showed the amounts of various items of operating costs (administrative expenses, financial expenses, impairment losses on assets), but JiuCe Company did not adduce evidence to prove the specifics of such losses. Under these circumstances, the court of second instance, based on JiuCe Company's statements on annual profit, in combination with the profit margin reflected in the Audit Report submitted by JiuCe Company during the second instance, determined in its discretion to find the expected benefits during the suspension period at an annual profit margin of 20%, and thus determined the amount of JiuCe Company's losses at RMB 4,493,643.03, which was not improper. The 2019 and 2020 annual audit reports and partial financial statements submitted by JiuCe Company in the retrial were explanations of its claim for losses during the suspension period based on the minimum annual processing volume. Although these exhibits showed a profit margin of over 30%, they could not directly reflect the losses during the suspension period and were unilateral evidence. Therefore, this part of the evidence is no longer considered. Furthermore, pursuant to Article 119 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "After a party breaches the contract, the other party shall take appropriate measures to prevent the aggravation of losses; if the other party fails to take appropriate measures so that the losses are aggravated, it may not claim damages for the aggravated part. The reasonable expenses incurred by the other party in preventing the aggravation of losses shall be borne by the breaching party," JiuCe Company had an obligation to prevent the aggravation of losses, and FengSheng Company should not be liable for aggravated losses. Based on the above, considering that JiuCe Company did not take measures to prevent the aggravation of losses during the period when FengSheng Company ceased taking delivery of gases, and taking into account factors such as the degree of fault of FengSheng Company, this court will not adjust the amount of losses determined by the court of second instance.

The expected benefits determined by the court of second instance were essentially JiuCe Company's losses during the period of cessation of taking delivery of gases. Although the description in the main text of the judgment as "processing fees during the suspension period" was inappropriate, the amount was properly determined and did not affect the assumption of liability by the parties. Therefore, this court will not adjust that item.

2. Regarding the determination of overdue payment liquidated damages on processing fees during the period of cessation of gas supply

JiuCe Company, based on the agreement on liability for breach of contract for delay in payment of processing fees under Article 6.1.3 of the processing contract, claimed liability for overdue payment liquidated damages on the processing fees during the suspension period. As mentioned above, JiuCe Company's claim for processing fees during the suspension period was not established, so its claim for overdue payment liquidated damages on such fees based on that clause was also not established. This court has already determined JiuCe Company's losses during the period of cessation of gas supply and will not support JiuCe Company's claim in this regard.

Additionally, the court of second instance calculated and handled the court fees of first and second instance together without distinguishing them, resulting in an unclear amount of court fees to be borne. This court corrects that as well.

In summary, JiuCe Company's retrial claim regarding liquidated damages is established and should be supported. The judgments of first and second instance were unclear in the determination of part of the facts and erroneous in the application of law, and are hereby corrected. Pursuant to Paragraph 1 of Article 214, Subparagraph 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 177, and Article 260 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 323 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Affirm Item 3 of the civil judgment (2020) Gan Min Zhong No. 143 of the Gansu High People's Court, i.e., "Gansu FengSheng Environmental Technology Co., Ltd. shall pay Jinchang JiuCe Industrial Gas Co., Ltd. processing fees of RMB 4,493,643.03 for the period of suspension of production from February 14, 2015 to July 31, 2017, within thirty days after this judgment becomes effective";

2. Set aside Item 2 of the civil judgment (2020) Gan Min Zhong No. 143 of the Gansu High People's Court, and affirm Item 1 of the civil judgment (2019) Gan 03 Min Chu No. 7 of the Jinchang Intermediate People's Court of Gansu Province, i.e., "Gansu FengSheng Environmental Technology Co., Ltd. shall pay Jinchang JiuCe Industrial Gas Co., Ltd. processing fees of RMB 8,652,289.71 for the period from October 10, 2013 to February 13, 2015, overdue payment liquidated damages of RMB 5,461,480.52 on such processing fees up to December 31, 2017, and overdue payment liquidated damages at a daily interest rate of 0.05% from January 1, 2018 until the date of payment of such processing fees, to be performed within thirty days after this judgment becomes effective";

3. Amend Item 1 of the civil judgment (2020) Gan Min Zhong No. 143 of the Gansu High People's Court to read: Dismiss the other claims of Jinchang JiuCe Industrial Gas Co., Ltd.

If the obligation to pay money is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the debt interest for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 260 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The court fee of first instance is RMB 256,918, of which RMB 145,809 shall be borne by Jinchang JiuCe Industrial Gas Co., Ltd. and RMB 111,109 shall be borne by Gansu FengSheng Environmental Technology Co., Ltd. The court fee of second instance is RMB 256,918, of which RMB 216,984 shall be borne by Jinchang JiuCe Industrial Gas Co., Ltd. and RMB 39,934 shall be borne by Gansu FengSheng Environmental Technology Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
